standard_prerequisites.name: The support of a finite type quasi-coherent module is closed, cited from the modules chapter, and the affine description of a finite type quasi-coherent module as the tilde of a finite module together with the closedness of supports over affine schemes
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the closedness of the support, in the cited form or by combining the affine statements.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma in the form that a stalk is zero exactly when its tensor product with the residue field is zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the second equivalence of part (2) and is used again at the end of the proof for the pullback.

standard_prerequisites.name: The stalk of a pullback module is the tensor product of the original stalk with the local ring, cited from the sheaves chapter, and the pullback of a finite type module is of finite type, cited from the modules chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the compatibility of supports with pullback to the residue fibre criterion of part (2).

core_obligations: Part (1): the closedness of the support is a reformulation of the cited modules chapter statement, which the author notes can also be assembled from the affine description of finite type modules and the closedness of supports over affine schemes (proof lines 915-920).
Part (2): the first equivalence is the definition of support, and the second follows from Nakayama's lemma applied to the stalk at the point (proof lines 922-927).

Part (3): the pullback of a finite type module is of finite type; for a point of the source with image the given point, the stalk of the pullback is the tensor product of the original stalk with the local ring, so tensoring with the residue field of the source point is nonzero exactly when tensoring the original stalk with the residue field of the image is nonzero, which by part (2) says exactly that the supports correspond (proof lines 928-943).
proof_roadmap: Quote closedness of the support and rewrite the support condition via Nakayama's lemma on residue fibres (proof lines 915-927).
Compare the residue fibres of the pullback with those of the original module at the image point to get the compatibility of supports (proof lines 928-943).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the three basic properties of the support of a finite type quasi-coherent module: closedness, detection on residue fibres of stalks, and compatibility with pullback (statement lines 895-913). The counted proof is short but complete: the first part is the cited closedness statement with an alternative assembly from affine pieces, the second records that the first equivalence is the definition while the second is Nakayama's lemma, and the third uses the description of the stalk of a pullback as a tensor product to reduce the support correspondence to the residue fibre criterion (proof lines 915-943). It is H2: the arguments are carried out in the counted span and the inputs are standard.
